text:
vivian: Heads-up — EU2 GPU onboarding is blocked. New firewall default-deny went out ~09:58 and nodes can't decrypt secrets (KMS 403).
marcus: Ugh. Any node logs?
vivian: Paste from one of the kubelet pods:
```
2026-03-23T09:59:12Z ERROR keystore: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:eu-west-2:111:key/abcd-1234
node: gpu-eu2-ctl-7
```
vivian: The keystore service is using privatelink to hit our KMS grant broker. The privatelink endpoint policy was tightened in the firewall roll.
ops-bot: alert: keystore-kms denied 403 x 42 in last 5m — https://ops/redwood/alerts/keystore-kms-403
ben: I think the privatelink policy was changed to block sts:AssumeRole from the privatelink service principal to force tighter audit boundaries. We didn't add an explicit grant for the keystore path.
kyra: We shipped the deny to close an audit egress hole; we wanted to ensure only shipper-bucket-access was allowed. Did we whitelist the keystore role?
ben: No — looks like a deny statement that matched the privatelink role and shadowed the prior allow.
marcus: Quick mitigation options? We need GPUs online for a production rollout in EU2 this afternoon.
oncall-sre: Two fast options: 1) revert the privatelink change (fast, but rolls back audit hardening) or 2) add an explicit KMS grant + update endpoint policy to allow s3/keystore path from privatelink only. Option 2 is safer and can be narrow.
kyra: We prefer option 2. Revert only if option 2 fails. Approving emergency grant with short TTL.
vivian: I'll open a short-lived grant and patch endpoint policy. Proposed CLI to add a grant:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/keystore-eu2 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::111:role/keystore-privatelink --operations Decrypt --name "temp-onboard-grant"
```
vivian: And endpoint patch (minimal change):
```
# add statement allowing keystore-privatelink to call kms:Decrypt
aws ec2 modify-vpc-endpoint --vpc-endpoint-id vpce-0abcd --policy-document file://vpce-keystore-allow.json
```
ben: I'll stage the endpoint policy change and hand it to infra for apply. We'll lock the grant TTL to 4 hours.
marcus: Watch for audit shipper gaps — will we lose logs while this is in flight?
kyra: The audit shipper uses a privatelink mirror to a central SIEM; that path remains allowed for shipper-bucket, but the tighter policy accidentally matched privatelink role. Fixing the endpoint policy should not break shipper. Still, keep an eye on kinesis/s3 delivery metrics.
oncall-sre: I'll put a short synthetic check in place to monitor keystore Decrypt success and GPU node ready state. If >30 nodes still fail after 10m, we escalate to rollback.
ops-bot: deploy: endpoint-policy-change requested by ben at 10:26 — https://deploy/redwood/1234
vivian: Running the create-grant now. Will post outcomes.
vivian: Grant created (id g-0xdeadbeef) — testing on one node.
vivian: Test node decrypt succeeded, kubelet pulled secrets, node joined the cluster. :tada:
ben: Patching endpoint policy and setting grant TTL to 4h. Pushing as canary to eu2-edge-az1.
marcus: Cost note: adding a regional mirror for audit to avoid extra egress in future could add ~$150/day in S3 costs — FYI for product/cost teams.
kyra: Add to audit hardening PR as a TODO — prefer retention over risking onboarding.
oncall-sre: Monitoring — started 10:40. So far 12/16 pending nodes recovered after grant+policy patch. Will close thread when all recovered or if rollback needed.
vivian: Thanks team — will follow-up with a short postmortem and a suggested policy snippet for the keystore path.
ben: I'll namespace a more explicit allow for keystore in the endpoint policy and add tests to the privatelink CI to prevent accidental denial.
marcus: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: resolved? waiting for human close — https://ops/redwood/alerts/keystore-kms-403
